author: David Jordan
title: Sweeping permitting overhaul passes Senate, on to House
summary: Roll Call reports the Senate passed the permitting bill on Thursday night and that it seemingly has the votes in the House, with Speaker Johnson saying the week before that it can pass there.

quote.text: The bill now moves on to the House, where it seemingly has the votes to pass.
quote.speaker: David Jordan, reporter, Roll Call

author: Kaia Hubbard
title: Senate passes bipartisan permitting reform bill designed to boost energy projects
summary: CBS reports the 62-33 Senate passage and says the bill faces an uncertain House future over transmission provisions and Democratic objections.

quote.text: This bill is years in the making
quote.speaker: Sen. John Thune, Senate Majority Leader, as quoted by CBS News

author: Garrett Downs
title: Senate passes BAAJA permitting reform bill backed by AI, energy sectors
summary: CNBC reports the 62-33 Senate vote split Democrats and that the bill must still clear the House before reaching President Trump.

quote.text: No big, bipartisan bill is going to be perfect for everyone, but we have a real opportunity to make electricity more affordable for families.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., in a statement to CNBC

author: Leah Bowers
title: Permitting bill passes through the Senate despite some opposition
summary: Deseret News reports the Senate vote, says negotiators hope to enact the bill in the lame-duck session, and carries Sen. Lee's defense of its data center provisions against critics.

quote.text: BAAJA actually makes data centers pay more to interconnect to the grid to ensure other customers’ rates don’t increase
quote.speaker: Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, as quoted by Deseret News

author: Levi Rickert
title: Despite Strong Tribal Opposition, U.S. Senate Approves BAAJA in Late-Night Vote
summary: Native News Online reports passage over Tribal opposition to Section 106 changes, carries Sen. Padilla's no-vote statement, and says the House is on recess until Nov. 30.

quote.text: The bill threatens Tribal sovereignty, and I am deeply concerned that it could allow the destruction of ancestral lands, sacred places, and cultural resources
quote.speaker: Sen. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., in a statement quoted by Native News Online

author: Nico Portuondo and Anthony Cruz
title: Senate passes landmark permitting deal
summary: Politico reports Speaker Johnson told it he would first try to pass the Senate bill under suspension of the rules and, failing that, bring it up under a rule.

quote.text: It may be a suspension bill, but if not, we'll do it by rule.
quote.speaker: Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., as quoted by Politico

author: Ari Natter
title: Senate Passes Landmark Bill to Overhaul US Energy Permitting
summary: Bloomberg reports House Natural Resources Chairman Westerman doubts there is time to change the bill, and that Jeffries and some Republicans have said they want changes.

quote.text: If the Senate gets it done then I think that’s what we’ll have to pass in the House
quote.speaker: Rep. Bruce Westerman, R-Ark., House Natural Resources chairman, as quoted by Bloomberg

author: Stewart Huntington
title: Affordability and jobs act passes Senate
summary: ICT reports Tribal advocates are turning to the House after the Senate vote, and carries the NDN Collective's call for the House to vote against the bill.

quote.text: The House still has the chance to do the right thing and vote against BAAJA, allowing the next Congress to take up permitting reform
quote.speaker: Wizipan Garriot, president of NDN Collective, as quoted by ICT

author: Christine Peterson
title: Senate Passes BAAJA, the Massive Permitting Bill That Will Expedite Development on Public Lands
summary: Outdoor Life reports the 62-33 passage, conservation and Tribal concerns about public lands and data centers, and that any House change would require another Senate vote.

quote.text: I negotiated the deal based on what was actually possible to get signed into law
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., in an email to Outdoor Life

title: U.S. Chamber: Senate Vote on Permitting Bill Marks Turning Point for American Energy and Infrastructure
summary: The Chamber welcomed Senate passage and urged House members to pass the bill quickly and send it to the President.

quote.text: We now urge members in the House to quickly pass and send this legislation to the President's desk so crucial projects can finally move forward.
quote.speaker: Neil Bradley, executive vice president and chief policy officer, U.S. Chamber of Commerce

title: API Applauds Senate Passage of Bipartisan Permitting Reform Legislation
summary: API welcomed Senate passage of S. 5653 and credited the four sponsors, without addressing House timing.

quote.text: Today’s bipartisan Senate vote marks a major breakthrough on historic permitting reforms that would deliver more affordable energy for consumers, cut costly delays, and build much-needed critical infrastructure.
quote.speaker: Mike Sommers, president and CEO, American Petroleum Institute

title: Senate Permitting Bill Remains Unacceptable
summary: NRDC said it opposes the Senate-passed bill and urged the House to reject it and try again next year.

quote.text: The House should not pass a bill that gives President Trump a blank check to reward oil and gas companies and data center developers.
quote.speaker: Manish Bapna, president and CEO, NRDC

title: Statement on U.S. Senate passage of permitting reform legislation
summary: EDF said the bill gets some things right on transmission and data center costs, regretted that the Senate adopted no improvements, and urged the House to make changes.

quote.text: we urge the House to make meaningful improvements as it considers the legislation this session
quote.speaker: Fred Krupp, president, Environmental Defense Fund

title: Heinrich: Senate Passage of Landmark Bipartisan Permitting Deal Will Lower Electricity Bills, Hold Data Centers Accountable, Create Over One Hundred Thousand Jobs, Reduce Carbon Emissions
summary: Heinrich, a lead sponsor, welcomed Senate passage and said the bill must still pass the House before reaching the President.

quote.text: I'm proud of what we've accomplished. Now let's get this bill across the finish line and signed into law.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M.

outlet: Senate Environment and Public Works Committee (Chairman Capito)
title: Capito Commends BAAJA Passage, Thanks Supporters and Urges House Approval
summary: Capito's post-passage floor speech urged House colleagues to act quickly when they return and send the bill to President Trump.

quote.text: I hope our colleagues in the House will act quickly.
quote.speaker: Sen. Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va., EPW Chairman

author: Diana DiGangi
title: Permitting reform bill heads to House as Democratic divisions persist
summary: Utility Dive reports the 62-33 vote (47 Republicans, 15 Democratic caucus members) and Democratic divisions over whether to take the bill now or wait for the next Congress.

quote.text: There will be no better deal on the table
quote.speaker: Rep. Scott Peters, D-Calif., in a statement quoted by Utility Dive

author: Dan McCarthy
title: Senate OKs permitting bill that would boost clean and dirty energy
summary: Canary reports the Senate vote, the split among decarbonization advocates, and Sierra Club's call for the House to reject the bill.

quote.text: must reject the Senate’s fast-tracked bill and demand debate and consideration to deliver for the people, not corporate polluters and Donald Trump
quote.speaker: Loren Blackford, executive director, Sierra Club, as quoted by Canary Media

title: WHAT THEY ARE SAYING: Send the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act to President Trump’s Desk
summary: The White House release quotes President Trump on Senate passage and says the House now has the opportunity to finish the job and send the bill to his desk.

quote.text: Last night, landmark permitting reform legislation passed the Senate. It’s one of the biggest things that you will see.
quote.speaker: President Donald J. Trump, as quoted in the White House release

title: New Democrat Coalition Leaders Release Statement on Senate Passage of Bipartisan Permitting Reform
summary: The coalition's leaders welcomed Senate passage, regretted that the managers' amendment was left out, and said they would seek changes in the House while urging action before year end.

quote.text: We are deeply disappointed that amendments, including the bipartisan Manager’s Amendment, were held up procedurally and left out of this bill.
quote.speaker: Rep. Brad Schneider, D-Ill., Rep. Nikki Budzinski, D-Ill., and Rep. Scott Peters, D-Calif., New Democrat Coalition leaders

outlet: Senate Environment and Public Works Committee (Ranking Member Whitehouse)
title: Whitehouse Cheers Senate Passage of Landmark Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
summary: Whitehouse, a lead sponsor, welcomed Senate passage and said the bill now heads to the House.

quote.text: Americans will quickly begin getting some relief on their energy bills if the House follows suit.
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., EPW Ranking Member

author: Emily Pontecorvo
title: The Permitting Bill’s Next Battleground
summary: Heatmap lays out the House path: Johnson's plan to try suspension the week after Thanksgiving, the two-thirds math, Democratic splits, and the Senate sponsors' wish to pass the stalled tribal amendment later.

quote.text: said earlier this week that he would try to pass BAAJA under suspension, a process that would send it straight to the floor for a vote the week after Thanksgiving
quote.speaker: Emily Pontecorvo, reporter, Heatmap, describing Speaker Mike Johnson
